note: Texts for women. The programme engine and ids are the same as the men's version; only the words change.

tracks.title: Sexual Health and Sensation
tracks.text: Full-strength contractions; lying, sitting and standing in every session. Knowing the muscle better can support sensation and control during sex.
tracks.note: It is not a medical treatment; no particular result is promised.

tracks.title: Control and Coordination
tracks.text: Coordination of quick contractions and full release, matching with the breath, awareness of relaxation.

tracks.title: Leaks and Bladder Control
tracks.text: Slow holds, quick contractions and squeezing before a cough, sneeze or lift (the Knack).

tracks.title: Recovery After Giving Birth
tracks.text: A gentle start, beginning lying down and progressing to standing, plus Knack practice.
tracks.note: Unlocks only if your doctor or midwife has approved it. Don't exercise if you have pain, bleeding or a problem with stitches.
Recommended if you think your pelvic floor may be holding tension. It's a good idea to see a gynaecologist or a pelvic floor physiotherapist.

questions.text: Do you have ongoing pain or a feeling of pressure in your pelvis, perineum (between the anus and vagina), groin or anus?
Do you have pain during or after sex?
Do you leak urine when you cough, sneeze or jump?

result.relaxText: Your answers suggest your pelvic floor may be holding tension. In that case, squeezing exercises can make discomfort worse. We suggest seeing a gynaecologist or a pelvic floor physiotherapist before you start training.
result.dribbleText: A short squeeze before a cough, sneeze or lift (the Knack) can help reduce leaks.
